<!--
WRITTEN 2026-08-11 (Luciano). This figure exists to draw one sentence of 04_results, the one that
says the channel count and the noise level enter only through their ratio. Until today that sentence
cited a chunk of figure_5.Rmd that does not exist in that file; the measurement was rebuilt in the
collapse chunk of figure_5_Nch.Rmd and this is its display. It is also the licence for the body
figure to be four panels in one row: if the two axes are one axis, then tau_int and the acquisition
interval are the whole parameterization and there is no third number to draw.

THE RATIO. r = S_tilde / N_ch, the instrumental noise over one channel time constant divided by the
number of channels, which is the instrumental variance against the gating variance those channels
carry. S_tilde is the label over ten (noise_units.R); the ten cancels out of any statement about the
collapse and only moves r by a decade, so it is converted here for the same reason as everywhere,
because the number is shown.

WHAT IS DRAWN, and why it is the persuasive form. Each line is one channel count at one acquisition
interval, swept over the instrumental noise: 4 x 7 = 28 lines per panel, the same 28 in both columns.
On the left they are drawn against S_tilde and they fan out, four visibly separate curves per colour,
one per channel count, each displaced from the next by a decade. On the right they are drawn against
r and the four merge, so 28 lines are drawn and 7 are visible. Nothing is fitted, rescaled or
normalized between the columns; the only difference is the horizontal coordinate.

The lines are NOT a model. They join cells of the battery in order of noise, which is a design sweep,
and the four channel counts are separate simulations of different preparations, so their landing on
one curve is a measurement and not a construction.

THE NUMBER IN EACH RIGHT PANEL is the residual disagreement, computed only on the cells that share an
r EXACTLY at the same interval (8 values of r, 56 groups), so it involves no interpolation at all.
Median 1 to 2 per cent everywhere. The one large maximum is R, and it is the ill-conditioned corner
that figure_5.Rmd's header records as its pending edit: N_ch = 10^4 at Delta_tilde = 1, where R
disagrees by 88 per cent and least squares, not drawn here, by a factor of 13.6. Drop that one cell
and R falls to 23 per cent, LSE to 99. Maxima over the whole ladder, all cells / dropping the corner
cell / dropping the whole coarsest interval: LSE 1256-99-99, ILSE 5-5-5, NR 29-29-29, INR 12-12-9,
R 88-23-23, MR 11-11-11, VR 16-16-9, IR 8-7-4, all in per cent. Which of the three columns is quoted
has to be said, because they differ; 04_results quotes the third.

THE BOOTSTRAP IS DRAWN, added 2026-08-11 (Luciano), and it is what makes the agreement checkable:
a claim that two curves coincide means nothing without the width of the points being compared. The
bars are the bootstrap quantiles of each cell, hi and lo of the same statistic, median width 3 per
cent (hi/lo) and much the same for every member.
  READ IT AGAINST THE AGREEMENT. The median disagreement at matched r is 1 per cent, so the four
  channel counts land closer together than any one of them is known, which is the strongest form the
  claim can take. Of the maxima, ILSE at 5 and IR at 8 per cent are the excursions 56 groups of
  3-per-cent points produce on their own and should not be read as structure; INR at 12 and R at 88
  are not, and R's is the single ill-conditioned cell.
  THE IR ROW IS NOW HONEST ON A FREE SCALE. Its whole cloud is 0.98 to 1.08 and its bars span very
  nearly that, so what the panel shows is the estimation floor and not a departure of the member.
  This is the same fact figure_5.Rmd's header gives as the decisive reason the BODY figure keeps one
  shared y ("a free axis draws the bootstrap at full panel height"); here the free scale is wanted
  and the bars are what keep it from lying.
  THE TOP ROW HAS NO BARS AND THAT IS THE SOURCE, NOT A CHOICE. figure_4_data.R:129-133 passes the
  scalars through with probit == "mean" while the spectrum pass keeps probit in (mean, quantile), so
  tau_int reaches the CSV without its quantiles. Getting them is not a one-line change: the scalar
  branch has to keep the quantile rows, fig4_shape_scal has to stop collapsing them into a single
  mean, and the cell_scalars CSV needs lo/hi columns, after which figure_4's source data has to be
  re-emitted from the 3.3 GB of inputs. Worth doing if a referee asks; not worth doing for this.

PATCHWORK, NOT A FACET GRID, and that is not cosmetic. The five rows are five different quantities
and the two columns are two different abscissas, so a facet grid can offer one y title and one x
title for all of them, which is how the first version came to carry "top row: tau_int / rows below:
distortion" down its side. Each panel now names its own quantity and its own abscissa. What stays
shared is deliberate: the y scale WITHIN a row, because the two columns are the same cells and a
free scale would fake a difference where the only difference is the horizontal coordinate, and the x
scale down a column. The right panel of each row keeps its ticks and carries the row's y title in
transparent ink, because patchwork gives the two columns equal total width and without the reserved
title the right panel comes out wider than the left by exactly that much.

GROUP ON THE DECADE, NOT ON r. Every noise and every channel count in the battery is a power of ten,
but the double S_tilde/N_ch is not bit-identical between (0.01, 10) and (0.1, 100), so grouping on it
splits matched cells apart and understates the collapse. It cost 76 per cent instead of 88 for R on
the first run of this file.

THE TOP ROW IS THE FIGURE 5 AXIS ITSELF, tau_int of the least-squares residual, and it collapses
too, to within 3.5 per cent. That is the part that matters most: it says the horizontal axis of the
body figure already absorbs both design axes, so a reader who measures tau_int on their own record
has, without knowing it, measured r.

Anchor, source files and member labels as in figure_5.Rmd. Do not re-derive anything here.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages({ library(tidyverse) })
```

```{r data}
source("noise_units.R")  # the one definition of S_tilde and of when to convert

SRC <- "../figure_4_source_data"
rd  <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(SRC, f), skip = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

LAB  <- c(nonlinearsqr = "ILSE", macro_INR = "INR", macro_R = "R", macro_IR = "IR")
KEEP <- names(LAB)

tau <- rd("figure_4_source_data_cell_scalars.csv") %>%
  filter(param == "lag", anchor == "pool", algo == "nonlinearsqr") %>%
  transmute(noise = as.numeric(noise), Num_ch, interval_in_tau, tau_int = v)

# hi and lo are the bootstrap quantiles of the same statistic, which the spectrum pass keeps and the
# scalar pass does not (figure_4_data.R:129-133 filters the scalars to probit == "mean"). So the four
# member rows below can carry an estimation error and the tau_int row cannot. Said in the caption.
spec <- rd("figure_4_source_data_spectrum.csv") %>%
  filter(anchor == "pool", param == "mag", algo %in% KEEP) %>%
  transmute(member = unname(LAB[algo]), noise = as.numeric(noise), Num_ch,
            interval_in_tau, mag = m, mag_lo = lo, mag_hi = hi) %>%
  filter(is.finite(mag), mag > 0)

# One long table of the five quantities the figure stacks: the axis of Figure 5 itself, which is a
# property of the least-squares fit alone and so has no member, then the four members' distortion.
ROWS <- c("tau[int]", unname(LAB))
qty <- bind_rows(
  tau %>% transmute(noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, quantity = "tau[int]", y = tau_int,
                    y_lo = NA_real_, y_hi = NA_real_),
  spec %>% inner_join(tau, by = c("noise", "Num_ch", "interval_in_tau")) %>%
    transmute(noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, quantity = member, y = mag,
              y_lo = mag_lo, y_hi = mag_hi)
) %>%
  mutate(S = dimensionless_noise(noise),          # label / 10
         r = S / Num_ch,                          # the ratio the collapse is in
         # Group on the DECADE, not on r itself. Every noise and every channel count in the battery
         # is a power of ten, but S/N_ch is not bit-identical between (0.01, 10) and (0.1, 100), so
         # grouping on the double silently splits matched cells apart and understates the collapse.
         r_key = round(log10(S)) - round(log10(Num_ch)),
         quantity = factor(quantity, levels = ROWS),
         d = factor(sprintf("%g", interval_in_tau),
                    levels = sprintf("%g", sort(unique(interval_in_tau)))),
         curve = interaction(interval_in_tau, Num_ch, drop = TRUE))

# The residual disagreement, on cells that share an r EXACTLY at the same interval. No interpolation.
# The agreement is only meaningful against the estimation error of the points being compared, so the
# bootstrap width travels with it: boot is the median hi/lo of one point, in the same units as the
# spread, and a spread below it is agreement to better than either point is known.
resid <- qty %>%
  group_by(quantity, interval_in_tau, r_key) %>% filter(n() > 1) %>%
  summarise(spread = max(y) / min(y), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(quantity) %>%
  summarise(n_groups = n(), med = median(spread), max = max(spread), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(qty %>% group_by(quantity) %>%
              summarise(boot = median(y_hi / y_lo), .groups = "drop"), by = "quantity")

cat(sprintf("figure_5_S1: %d lines per panel (%d intervals x %d channel counts), %d cells\n",
            n_distinct(qty$curve), n_distinct(qty$interval_in_tau), n_distinct(qty$Num_ch),
            n_distinct(qty[c("noise", "Num_ch", "interval_in_tau")])))
resid %>% as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)

AX <- c(raw = "against the instrumental noise",
        scaled = "against the noise per channel")
long <- bind_rows(mutate(qty, axis = "raw", x = S),
                  mutate(qty, axis = "scaled", x = r)) %>%
  mutate(axis = factor(unname(AX[axis]), levels = unname(AX)))

# one label per right-hand panel, placed by the panel's own corner
notes <- resid %>%
  transmute(quantity, axis = factor(AX[["scaled"]], levels = unname(AX)),
            lab = sprintf("at matched r:  %.0f%% median,  %.0f%% max",
                          100 * (med - 1), 100 * (max - 1)))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 7.8}
suppressMessages({ library(patchwork) })

# ONE PLOT PER PANEL, assembled with patchwork, because the axes of this figure are genuinely
# different from one another and a facet grid can only carry one title per direction. The previous
# version wrote "top row: tau_int / rows below: distortion" down the y and "left column: S_tilde /
# right column: r" along the x, which is two composite labels standing in for five y axes and two x
# axes. Each panel now names its own quantity and its own abscissa.
# What is still shared, and deliberately: the y scale within a row (the two columns are the SAME
# cells, so a different scale would fake a difference where the only difference is the abscissa),
# and the x scale down a column. So the right panel of each row keeps its tick marks, for reading
# values without crossing the figure, and drops the title the left one already carries.

PANEL_Y <- c("tau[int]" = "memory in the LS residual",
             ILSE = "distortion, ILSE", INR = "distortion, INR",
             R = "distortion, R", IR = "distortion, IR")
X_LAB <- list(raw    = expression("instrumental noise  "*widetilde(S)),
              scaled = expression("noise per channel  r = "*widetilde(S)/N[ch]))

base_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 7.5),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 7.5, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5,
                                  margin = margin(b = 2)),
        plot.margin = margin(1, 2, 1, 1))

# y limits are set from the row, not from the panel, so that the two columns are comparable
ylims <- qty %>% group_by(quantity) %>%
  summarise(lo = min(c(y, y_lo), na.rm = TRUE),
            hi = max(c(y, y_hi), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

panel <- function(q, side, top = FALSE, bottom = FALSE) {
  dd <- filter(qty, quantity == q) %>% mutate(x = if (side == "raw") S else r)
  yl <- filter(ylims, quantity == q)
  p <- ggplot(dd, aes(x, y, colour = d, group = curve)) +
    { if (q != "tau[int]") geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey45") } +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.85) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = y_lo, ymax = y_hi), linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.55,
                   na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_point(size = 0.45) +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = 10^seq(-6, 6, 2), labels = scales::label_log(digits = 2)) +
    scale_y_log10(limits = c(yl$lo, yl$hi)) +
    scale_colour_viridis_d(name = expression(widetilde(Delta)), option = "D", end = 0.92) +
    labs(x = if (bottom) X_LAB[[side]] else NULL,
         # the right panel carries the SAME title in transparent ink: patchwork gives the two
         # columns equal total width, so without it the right panel is wider than the left by the
         # width of the title and the two columns stop being comparable at a glance.
         y = PANEL_Y[[q]],
         title = if (top) c(raw = "four curves per colour", scaled = "one curve per colour")[[side]]
                 else NULL) +
    base_theme
  if (side == "scaled") {
    note <- filter(resid, quantity == q)
    p <- p + annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.04, vjust = 1.25, size = 2.0,
                      colour = "grey25",
                      lineheight = 0.95,
                      label = sprintf("at matched r: %.0f%% median, %.0f%% max\n%s",
                                      100 * (note$med - 1), 100 * (note$max - 1),
                                      if (is.na(note$boot)) "no bootstrap in the source"
                                      else sprintf("bootstrap width %.0f%%",
                                                   100 * (note$boot - 1))))
  }
  if (side == "scaled") p <- p + theme(axis.title.y = element_text(colour = NA))
  if (!bottom) p <- p + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
  p
}

QS <- levels(qty$quantity)
plots <- unlist(lapply(seq_along(QS), function(i)
  lapply(c("raw", "scaled"), function(sd)
    panel(QS[i], sd, top = i == 1, bottom = i == length(QS)))), recursive = FALSE)

g <- wrap_plots(plots, ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7), legend.key.height = unit(9, "pt"))

ggsave("Figure_5_S1.pdf", g, width = 7.0, height = 7.8, device = cairo_pdf)
g
```

```{r numbers}
cat("how far apart the four channel counts are on the RAW axis, so that the left column has a\n",
    "number too: ratio of the largest to the smallest y at one S_tilde and one interval\n", sep = "")
qty %>% group_by(quantity, interval_in_tau, S) %>% filter(n() > 1) %>%
  summarise(spread = max(y) / min(y), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(quantity) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), med = median(spread), max = max(spread), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)

cat("\nthe same cells regrouped by r, which is the right column (this is the collapse):\n")
resid %>% as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)

cat("\nand with the ill-conditioned corner (N_ch = 10^4 at Delta_tilde = 1) left out:\n")
qty %>% filter(!(Num_ch == 10000 & interval_in_tau == 1)) %>%
  group_by(quantity, interval_in_tau, r_key) %>% filter(n() > 1) %>%
  summarise(spread = max(y) / min(y), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(quantity) %>%
  summarise(n_groups = n(), med = median(spread), max = max(spread), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)
```
